$comment: CANONICAL CONTEXT CONTRACT — the single definition of TargetEntity, CareStage, IntentType and ContextResolutionStatus shared by Java, Python and the response contract. Both runtimes assert their enums against this file, so a value added on one side without the other fails the parity test instead of drifting silently. Same generated-copy discipline as the rule registry: never edit a copy, run DevTools/sync_triage_rule_registry.py.

targetEntity.$comment: Who the session is about. Never null — an absent answer is UNKNOWN, and contradictory evidence is CONFLICTED. Exactly one primary target entity per triage session.

legacyStageMapping.$comment: Legacy POSTPARTUM is ambiguous: it named the maternal stage, but a postpartum session may also be about the newborn. It maps ONLY when the target is MOTHER; with BABY or an unresolved target it must NOT be auto-mapped — resolve the target first.

intentType.$comment: Only SYMPTOM_TRIAGE and FOLLOW_UP_ANSWER may produce a triage colour. GENERAL_HEALTH_INFORMATION and SOURCE_LOOKUP answer a question about material and must never be reported as an assessment of the user. EMERGENCY_HELP does not itself decide RED — the Global Safety Gate does.

contextResolutionStatus.$comment: blocksSymptomQuestions lists the states in which the Question Planner may ask ONLY a clarification question. Asking a symptom question before the target is known risks asking the mother about the baby, or applying a maternal threshold to an infant.

resolutionSource.$comment: Where a resolved value came from, in precedence order (highest first). Recorded so an audit can show whether a value was stated by the user or merely inferred.
